The loaded census is first verified against this summary (artifact_count, zero_byte_count, first_at, last_at, max_burst, bursts, burst_size_histogram, primary_id): any mismatch is E_CENSUS_MISMATCH, a missing summary is E_CENSUS_UNDECLARED, and an unparseable or inverted burst clock is E_CENSUS_CLOCK rather than a silent skip. E_CHILD_OUTSIDE_WINDOW rejects any documented child whose started_at precedes window.from or finished_at exceeds window.to, so narrowing the window cannot hide an omitted child.

honest_limits: Every one of the 194 child artifacts in this coordinator session's store is 0 bytes with mtime within ~50 ms of birthtime. The artifact store therefore yields dispatch START times only; per-child FINISH times are unrecoverable for earlier waves. Real finish times exist only where a host completion notification supplied duration_ms (the six finished children above). Earlier-wave durations are NOT asserted here rather than fabricated. Filed as an observability defect in docs/backlog/GAPS.md.

The 194-artifact census proves a dispatch BURST cap, which is strong evidence but not identical to a concurrency proof: a burst bounds how many children were started together, not how many were simultaneously alive. The concurrency proof is the sweep over the four sessions with observed clocks in this window (peak 3 children / 4 sessions). In this window the interval sweep peaks at 3 children / 4 total sessions, so the concurrency cap holds with one child of headroom.
Earlier-wave role attribution is not asserted. Only sessions whose agent type the coordinator dispatched directly in this window are role-labelled.
Legacy OpenCode worktrees on this host are prior-session artifacts, preserved untouched. No live foreign coordinator was observed, and this attestation covers sessions on this host only.

Cancellation, event-wait and restart-recovery clauses are exercised by the deterministic ledger tests (tests/sessionLedger.test.mjs), which fail closed on missing finish records, contradictory status and time-order inversion. The host exposes no cancellation or restart API to this session, so those clauses are validated at the ledger-contract level, not by killing a live child.

The census is broader than the ledger window: 194 session-store artifacts versus 6 children documented here. Only in-window artifacts are cross-checked, so this receipt does NOT claim to document every child ever dispatched on this host. Widening window.from to the census start would require documenting all 194, which the 0-byte artifact defect makes impossible.
window_basis: from = birthtime of the first child dispatched in this wave (aaceb00b9092592a2, 19:01:37.767Z); to = the finish of the last child of this wave (the same session, which ran longest). The window deliberately covers THIS WAVE only. dispatch_census is a snapshot of the coordinator session's whole artifact store (194 artifacts back to 01:06:06.252Z, spanning earlier waves); the undocumented-child cross-check is scoped to the window, so artifacts outside it are not asserted to be children of this ledger. Children dispatched after window.to belong to the next wave and are not claimed here. The window itself remains SELF-DECLARED: E_CHILD_OUTSIDE_WINDOW proves documented children lie inside it, but no validator can prove the window was not narrowed to exclude an inconvenient dispatch. An auditor must compare window.from against the census's first in-wave burst (here the 3-child burst at 19:01:37.767Z) and confirm every census burst from that point to window.to is documented in sessions[].
